claim: contract_doc_drift: 187 findings across docs/standards/*.md — "doc references `X` but no match in project sources"
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06 against every flagged line. The rule treats a backticked token in a doc as a claim about this project's source symbols. docs/standards/ holds generic FORMAT STANDARDS, so its backticks are: (a) naming EXAMPLES and COUNTER-examples (coding.md:108 `parseRGBColor`, :116 `strName`/`iCount` — the latter explicitly forbidden); (b) C++/Qt idiom names in § 5.1/5.2, which a Python project will never contain (`std::make_unique`, `QSaveFile`, `qDebug`); (c) format vocabulary (`Kind:`, `Lanes:`, `Layman:`, `PROJ-NNNN`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, commit trailers `Co-Authored-By:`); (d) prose words that happen to be backticked (`yesterday`, `recently`, `size`); (e) citations into OTHER projects (roadmap-format.md:74 `roadmapdialog.cpp`, :591 `remotecontrol.cpp` — Ants Terminal, not this repo); (f) forward references to core modules coding.md § O1 itself names as not-yet-built (`supervisor`, `logbuffer`, `controller`) and P04 theme tokens (`accent`, `state_running`). None is a defect. The rule is meaningful against d…

claim: bandit B101 assert_used: 28 findings, all in tests/test_applog.py
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06: all 28 are LOW severity / HIGH confidence and every one is a pytest `assert` in tests/test_applog.py — bandit -f csv shows a single test_name value, assert_used. pytest's entire assertion mechanism is the bare `assert` statement, so the rule fires on correct test code by construction. The project already encodes this: pyproject.toml [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores] sets "tests/**" = ["S101", ...] for ruff's port of the same rule, scoped to tests only so the production rule keeps its teeth. bandit's own default severity floor (-ll, which audit_run uses) filters these to zero; they were only visible because this session re-ran bandit without the floor to prove the tool had actually analysed the tree rather than crashed. No production-code assert exists. Re-verify if a B101 ever appears under src/.

claim: deptry DEP002: PySide6, psutil, pytest, pytest-qt and ruff "defined as a dependency but not used in the codebase"
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06. Two distinct non-defects. (1) PySide6 and psutil are genuinely not imported yet, and that is the project's DELIBERATE state at P01: P01 is bootstrap only (three modules — __init__, __main__, applog — and CLAUDE.md § Module map says "No GUI until P02"). PySide6 lands with LWSM-1005 (P02, the vertical slice) and psutil with LWSM-1009/P05 and the PortProbe in P07. Removing either pin to satisfy the rule would undo pyproject.toml's load-bearing version reasoning (the PySide6 comment records that QProcess.setChildProcessModifier is absent in 6.11, which is why ADR-0003 exists). (2) pytest, pytest-qt and ruff are [project.optional-dependencies] dev tools, flagged only because the scan was pointed at src/ alone; a dev tool is invoked as a command, never imported. Re-verify after P02/P05 land: PySide6 or psutil still unimported THEN would be a real finding.

claim: vulture: unused method `_open` (applog.py:26) and unused function `_reset_logging` (test_applog.py:38), both 60% confidence
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06 by reading both sites. `_open` is an OVERRIDE of logging.FileHandler._open, called by the stdlib base class (FileHandler.__init__ and doRollover), never by this project — and it is the entire point of _NoFollowRotatingFileHandler: it re-opens with O_NOFOLLOW so a symlink planted at app.log cannot redirect the log (the LWSM-1026 hardening). Deleting it would silently restore the vulnerability. `_reset_logging` carries @pytest.fixture(autouse=True) on the line directly above its def (test_applog.py:38), so pytest invokes it for every test in the module by collection, not by a call site; it is what stops process-global logging state leaking between tests. Both are the documented vulture blind spot: framework-invoked callables have no textual caller. Re-verify only if either loses its framework hook (the decorator, or the base-class name).

claim: typos: `THM` should be `THEM` (docs/design.md ×6) and `mis` should be `miss`/`mist` (ROADMAP.md ×2)
rationale:
Verified 2026-08-06 by reading all eight lines. `THM` is a MERMAID NODE IDENTIFIER in design.md's architecture diagram — declared at line 50 as `THM[ThemeManager
palette to QPalette
+ style sheet]` and referenced on lines 73-77 as edge endpoints (`SD --> THM`, `THM --> MW`). Renaming it to THEM would be nonsense and would have to be done consistently across every edge or the diagram breaks. The two ROADMAP hits are `mis-detection` (line 353) and `mis-reporting` (line 744) — correct English use of the `mis-` prefix with a hyphen, which the dictionary check splits on the hyphen and then fails to recognise. Neither is a spelling error. Re-verify only if the diagram node is renamed.

claim: yamllint: ci.yml missing document start "---" (7:1), truthy value for `on:` (9:1), too few spaces before comment (35:73)
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06 against scripts/local-ci.sh:110, which invokes `yamllint -d relaxed .github/`. All three warnings exist only under yamllint's DEFAULT profile; the project deliberately runs the relaxed profile, which disables document-start, truthy and comment-spacing. This session's finding came from re-running yamllint without `-d relaxed`, i.e. against a stricter bar than the project adopted. The truthy one is additionally wrong on its merits: `on:` is GitHub Actions' required trigger key and cannot be written as a boolean-safe alternative. actionlint — the workflow-aware checker, which the same gate runs first — reports the file clean. Re-verify if the project ever drops `-d relaxed`.

claim: semgrep insecure-file-permissions: 0o700 on the state directory is "widely permissive", use 0o644
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06. The recommendation is more permissive than the code it flags: 0o644 is world-READABLE while 0o700 is owner-only, and this directory holds a log of the user's whole project inventory and layout. On a directory the execute bit is also what makes it traversable, so 0o644 would additionally make it unusable. Taking the advice would regress a finding this project fixed on purpose and would break tests/test_applog.py::test_state_dir_and_log_are_not_world_readable, which asserts exactly 0o700. The rule reads as written for regular files with no directory case. It began firing only because src/lwsm/applog.py::_prepare_state_dir now sets the mode via os.fchmod on a directory fd instead of Path.chmod — the mode itself is unchanged from the version semgrep passed clean. Suppressed inline with nosemgrep citing docs/audit-allowlist.md allowlist-005. Re-verify if the rule learns to distinguish a directory mode from a file mode.

claim: typos: `versoin` should be `version` in tests/test_main.py and CHANGELOG.md
rationale: Verified 2026-08-06: the misspelling is the test input, deliberately. tests/test_main.py::test_an_unknown_option_is_refused passes `--versoin` to main() to prove an unrecognised option now exits 2 with usage instead of being silently ignored, which is what the previous `"--version" in args` membership test did. Correcting the spelling would make the test assert the opposite of its purpose (`--version` is a VALID flag and would exit 0). The CHANGELOG hit is the same string quoted in the entry describing that fix. Both appeared on 2026-08-06 as a side effect of the FP02 fix, not as a defect. No suppression added: typos is not part of scripts/local-ci.sh, so a config file for a tool the gate does not run would be scope the project has not taken on. Re-verify only if typos joins the gate, at which point an allowlist entry for this one word is the fix.

claim: bandit B103 (HIGH): "Chmod setting a permissive mask 0o777 on file (state)" at tests/test_applog.py:481
rationale: Verified at tests/test_applog.py:478-495. The 0o777 IS the precondition under test: the test creates a world-writable state dir and asserts configure_logging() TIGHTENS it back to 0o700. The line already carries `# noqa: S103` for ruff's equivalent rule with the reason inline ("S103 is correct in general and inverted here, where 0o777 is the hostile state under test"). Bandit does not read ruff noqa comments, so it re-raises what the project already dismissed. Fixing the code would delete the regression test for an upgrade from a version that wrote 0755.

claim: vulture: 7 unused variables in src/lwsm/theme.py — accent_soft (46), attention (47), state_wrong_port (69), state_foreign (70), state_blocked (71), state_failed (72), cls (77)
rationale: Verified by reading src/lwsm/theme.py:40-80. All six named colours are FIELDS of the `Theme` dataclass, not local variables — vulture cannot see that a dataclass field is populated by the generated __init__ and read by every palette literal in THEMES. The four state_* fields are additionally documented as deliberately defined ahead of LWSM-1011: "adding the states later without the colours means re-opening every palette", and test_the_state_tokens_are_distinguishable_from_the_body_text asserts over all of them today. `cls` at line 77 is the bound first parameter of the `default()` classmethod. No dead code in any of the seven.

claim: mypy (unconfigured, global): 33 errors in src/ — arg-type 19, attr-defined 15, union-attr 5, import-untyped 2, assignment 2, call-overload 1
rationale: Each src/ site read and verified as typing-hygiene with no runtime path: scanner.py:1050/1060 union-attr on `self._source` is unreachable because line 1034 sets `self._disabled = source is None` and both methods return early on `_disabled`; scanner.py:305/320/323/346/351 follow from `_wrap()` being deliberately annotated `-> object`; scanner.py:471 `match.group(match.lastindex)` is guarded by the comment "exactly one alternation group can have matched"; registry.py:1216 is a re-binding of `index` that the next line None-checks; mainwindow.py:373 is a Protocol invariance artefact (ScanLike declares `projects` settable; ScanResult is a frozen dataclass) with identical runtime behaviour; ports.py:13 and supervisor.py:37 are missing psutil stubs, an environment fact. The project declares no [tool.mypy] section and scripts/local-ci.sh runs no type checker, so none of these is a gate regression.

All dictionary preference or domain vocabulary, not misspellings. "unparseable" and "unparsable" are both standard English; the project uses the -eable form consistently. "unparented" is the Qt term for a widget with no parent and is what CLAUDE.md's own supervisor/pool notes mean. "certifi" is the PyPI package name. "raison" is inside "raison d'etre". "criticals" is the project's noun for CRITICAL-severity findings, used in .claude/workflow.md's phase records. No project typos config exists, so these recur every run; a [default.extend-words] block in a _typos.toml would settle them.

claim: CORRECTION to the 2026-08-31 entry above: vulture's theme.py accent_soft (46) and attention (47) are NOT false positives
rationale: The earlier record dismissed all seven theme.py vulture hits on one rationale ("read by every palette literal in THEMES"). A review lane challenged the wording and it is wrong for two of them: a palette literal ASSIGNS a field, it does not read one. Verified by grep — accent_soft and attention appear only as the field declaration plus 8 assignments across the palettes, with zero readers in src/, scripts/ or tests/. The state_* fields ARE genuinely read (tests/test_theme.py:80 names state_wrong_port in the contrast sweep), so the original rationale holds for those five and for cls. accent_soft and attention are real dead fields, promised by design-look-and-feel.md:80, and are being filed as a roadmap item rather than suppressed. docs/audit-allowlist.md:300 carries the same wrong rationale and needs the same correction.
